instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: No league goal in seven top-flight seasons; a functional left-back whose value was delivery from wide. Would not be in a modern squad.
Joined Blackburn from Coventry in March 1993.
Sixteen goals from wide right in a sixth-placed side and a Scotland regular at the World Cup; his best season.
No goals in 18 starts; the physical game was still there and nothing else was.
Three injury-wrecked seasons at Tottenham followed. The collapse in starts is fitness, but he did genuinely decline as a defender.
Technically the best player at the club; the output never matched what he could do with a ball.
PFA Player of the Year; reading and recovery of a genuinely elite defender.
Thirty-six and barely able to train; the reading of the game was intact, the body was not.
Seven starts; injury rather than a fall in level.
Past his peak but still a top-class finisher and the leading scorer.
Three goals in 34 starts at Leeds. Not a barren run for a still-good striker; the finishing itself had gone.
Sixteen years old and physically ready for the division, which is why he played; the reading of the game came much later.
Marginalised under Kenny Dalglish and reduced to 20 starts.
PFA and FWA Player of the Year. Elite one-v-one dribbler and crosser; held short of 90 by how little he offered without the ball.
Six goals from midfield in a relegated side; the season that earned the Leeds move.
The 74 anchor is Davies at 32, when the physical game that got him an England cap was fully formed. At 20-22 he was a quick, raw forward and a worse player than the anchor.
The best version of him: direct, quick, and a genuine problem for full-backs in a title-challenging side.
A World Cup winner months earlier and among the best defenders in the world; a shade below his Milan peak but still elite, above Adams (88) in 1998/99.
Banned from late January after Selhurst Park. Rated on the football played, not the games missed.
Captain and champion again but visibly declining; retired at the end of the season aged 30.
Two years on and a different player: an energetic, ball-winning central midfielder in a seventh-placed side, capped by England the following year.
Fringe at Chelsea at 22 but already a competent top-flight full-back; went on to a long Premier League and Netherlands career.
Chronic back and shin problems; effectively his last season of regular football, at 25.
A seven-point rise in one season at 19-20: pace and finishing that already looked elite, 17 league goals and PFA Young Player. Held below the Cole 1993/94 anchor (86) on all-round game.
Fourteen goals and genuinely frightening in a straight line; the finishing never caught up with the pace.
Nine starts after the Leeds move; could not get in the side.
Sixteen years old and a cameo player; rated as the unformed teenager, not the England international he became.
